mechanism_claims.claim_text: MCP-2 and MCP-3 are human CC chemokine-family monocyte chemotactic proteins identified from MG-63 osteosarcoma cell supernatant by purification and peptide sequencing.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The local primary paper supports chemokine identity/partial sequence, not antimicrobial peptide MIC activity.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: MCP-2 and MCP-3 selectively attract monocytes in vitro with little or no neutrophil chemotactic activity under the tested conditions.

source_locator.figure_locator: Figure 4; values are averages of three independent experiments

mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay is leukocyte chemotaxis, not antimicrobial killing.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: MCP-2 and MCP-3 enhance gelatinase B release from adherent monocytes, while neutrophil gelatinase B release was not observed for MCP molecules.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper states the monocyte result qualitatively and says data are not shown; no numeric gelatinase intensity was extracted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Intradermal MCP-2 and MCP-3 administration in rabbits induces selective monocyte recruitment in vivo.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Histology establishes monocyte recruitment; it does not establish direct tumor killing or antimicrobial activity.
